To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the monitoring domain is a highly mature and competitive one, with many offerings, and that whilst the offerings have continued in their core monitoring capability and sophistication, there is less support for the solution designer to achieve loose coupling and high cohesion in the service management layer, and less support for the SLA requirements of the services the service management layer manages.

• Monitoring is a key enabler for SaaS assurance and is critical for meeting key business priorities, • Monitoring is often a critical part of an enterprise’s service management layer, and • The monitoring domain is still immature in its ability to support service management layers in specifying their monitoring needs in terms of SLAs.

the monitoring domain needs to move towards the following: 1) Monitoring as a service: Monitoring should be a consumable service, not just a set of software tools that are deployed and managed by the enterprise.

the provision of a Monitoring Service that is capable of being managed as a consumable service by a Service Management Layer.

how monitoring can be better integrated with the Service Management Layer, and how the Service Management Layer can specify its monitoring requirements in terms to the SLA the service it is managing is being offered against.
the development of a monitoring service that is SLA-oriented and consumable as part of an SLA.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a new monitoring model which is SLA-oriented and which can be used to support a monitoring service as a consumable service.

we are working towards a model where the monitoring configuration is specified as a service and the SLA requirements are specified as an SLA, both of which can be consumed and provisioned as part of the service management process for the SaaS application.
we are developing a prototype monitoring service which can provide monitoring as a consumable service.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Service Management Layer should be able to specify monitoring requirements in terms that the monitoring layer understands and that the monitoring layer should be able to provide a consumable service to the Service Management Layer that is SLA-oriented.
it is possible to provide a service-oriented interface to the configuration of a monitoring solution.
